author: fxeyes
text:
I think I've heard IF say something to the effect of since we don't
have any information on all time highs, we can't trade them. Since i'm
not so smart, my thinking is simpler. Since we know the general
direction of price, can't we just keep looking for trades in that
direction, as continuation engulfs? I did an exercise on the sp500, and
 it's insane how well rtm concepts worked. There's pretty much at least
 a bounce at every mpl, ls kink, qm, iQm, etc... pretty much all the
concepts of RTM. Phenomenal success rates. With good MM, i don't know
how much simpler trading can be. The mpls are particular noteworthy as
these tiny inconspicuous zones became the reversal area for the next
trend up. Too bad I've only learned most of these concepts in the past
couple of months. It looks like price is starting to capitulate and
blow off sometime this month. As IF notes, there's no information to
look for areas for reversal.

author: fxeyes
text:
After reading some journals this weekend and doing some reflection,
I'm realizing there's something fundamentally flawed with the way I read
 the charts and look for trades. Lots of pieces, but they're not always
 coming together, and I think its because my approach is wrong, and
getting lost in scale. If I'm not mistaken, we should be:

1. Finding the significant FLs at important levels.

- What constitutes as significant?

2. Find the currently relevant FLs.

- What's the correct way to draw and trace through the FLs?

3. Know when an engulf has taken place (and hasn't hit it's target).

- What's a proper engulf?

- How do i identify the correct target for a broken FL?

3. Know the where the target is.

4. Know where the best orders are for entry.

- How do you identify where there orders?

- How far can price retrace?

- How do you identify the last set of orders before a turn?

5. Tying all this together through scale.

The hard part is there's so many ways to interpret it, and so easy to
get wrong. But being hard doesn't mean impossible. The kink video has
been great but it feels like there's still a lot guessing going on
(maybe i'm not just not letting unclear trades go, but I'm also letting a
 lot of good trades go). I"ve been relying on money management will
get me through incorrect analysis or unclear trades. But Sali's journal
 has been eye opening, and made me rethink my approach and where my gaps
 are.

Lets get these answered once and for all through true understanding and
analysis with HW. No new trades until this FL reading is accurate and
instinctual. Sali and IF's journals will be my bibles for the next
couple of weeks. If anyone thinks I'm headed in the wrong direction,
please let me know!

author: fxeyes
text:
winnertrader wrote: Hi IF,

I left out the rectangles in the previous chart to avoid creating a mess.

I attached two new charts of EURAUD below. My main problem is knowing
which swings to draw LS from especially when we have multiple back and
forth moves in the same area.

I've been thinking more about your troubles with these LS lines, and I
think your trouble is mixing up the lines between different time frames.
 Im reiterating stuff being said in the video and video forum (i
rewatched em), but I'll try to re-interpret it in a way that'll
hopefully help you.

Starting with a blank chart:

1. Drawing your major lines, at the extremes, where price has crossed it
 at least once. These are the lines that cut across all the way the
charts. The obvious stuff. Use judgement call of how far to go back as
 your TFs get smaller. There shouldn't be too many of these.

2. This one is trickier and you'll just have to practice and find a way
that works for you. The tops and bottoms of FLs that broke an important
 FL are important. But when price crosses price alot, it's leads to a
lot of lines. So if it looks important, draw a line across the chart.
If you're unsure, maybe only if it's been crossed recently.

3. Include the rest: PCP, Cm breaks, etc...Again same as two, maybe only
 include recently crossed ones, unless it looks really important.

4. Any other areas that seem to stand out, given what price is currently doing.

5*. I'll also throw in areas where price swings are at least semi-major
 and tends to swing a lot, if it hasn't been picked up by any of the
above (which is unlikely). The area will need more 'touches' the lower
the timeframe. So for example, in Mn it needs at least 3 touches. In
Wk it needs at least 5 touches. etc... These numbers can change
relative to the chart (charts that whipsaw back and forth will naturally
 have alot of touches. For example USDJPY vs USDCAD in Mn chart.

These should be all your major lines. For lines that you are not sure
about, just leave it out for now. I'll naturally be picked up in a lower
 tf. Then go and find your kinks. If you're not sure about something,
just use a judgement call. Don't worry too much about being wrong.
Here's an example from a chart that crosses alot

1

2

3

4

I think your chart looks pretty good! So maybe you were already on your way to figuring this stuff out.

I dont feel like I'm an expert at this, but i think you might be over
complicating things trying to be perfect. I kinda feel like i've over
done it already, and a number of the lines was better left to the lower
time frame, but its no worries. Maybe I'll dive into the LTF and adjust
 if needed. You just have to make a judgement call when you;re not
sure. Do you want to be more cautious so you won't miss a trade (but
will make your reading more difficult because you have so many lines),
or do you want a clean chart so the reading becomes easier?

Thank you for the insight IF! Between Sali's achievement of figuring
out the market through the same resources we have (probably less since
he doesn't appear to use the video concepts), and Ysbail's recent
improvements through study, I'm inspired to use your teachings to look
behind the covers of price and see what's going on underneath. I have
an odd way of learning; i need to know all the pieces, play with them
and see how they all work individually, before I can put them all
together. I've played with enough of the pieces and seen them in action
 in live trading to have a good idea of what they're about. But there
are some questions and uncertainty about them that i think is causing
hesitation and second guessing. I also have a theory of how the market
works. I seems like a good time to stop and do some intense studying to
 answer these questions. I'm going to list them out here for myself as a
 guide for my study, but feel free to offer any guidance where you see
fit =)

Flag Limits

1. How do I correctly identify FLs, so I can find the correct engulfs
and targets? I've been confused by a couple of styles:[/li]

a. Finding the kinks through major S/R lines.

i. If i'm trying to follow the FL breaks, how do i identify with FL to 'start' with?

ii. Or do I just find the last FL that breaks on the right side? If so,
 how do I draw the FL when price is choppy through the line?

b. I've also seen people draw FLs based on the last FL that's been holding price, then trace through it, which seems more local.

i. In this case, was there already an engulf somewhere that's offering guidance for the trade?

ii. Were they tying it in with a major s/r further to the left?

2.

PAZs

1. I understand there are PAZs in between the spaces of MPLs, but the
PAZs that stand out to me are the ones through symmetry, which seems to
be through s/r. I need further study of PAZs through MPLs (and I assume
FLs)

2. Do those concepts already naturally intermix?

2. How do i identify trades within a PAZ? Lets say a PAZ engulfs one
way, how far can price retrace (within the context of the last FL)
before going to the next FL?

Engulfs

1. I guess I need to a better understanding of FLs and targets first.

2. Sali had an interesting concept of FLs engulfing within an engulf, not necessarily always at the edge of it.

3. I think i need to train myself to look for these engulfs first for trade ideas.

Entries

1. Instead of looking at all the possible sets of orders and trading
each as price approaches, there seems to be a of figuring out where the
last set of orders are before price turning (and this may not always be
the last set of untouched orders, i think).

2. Should i only enter at mpls/qm/ls? If so, what makes them tradable,
do they have a particular structure? If seen price bounce at really odd
 looking patterns. Were they 'valid' or were they simply just noise
between the true mpls?

QM

1. Too often I've missed great QM trades because I was waiting it to
the neckline, but price turns before then. Why? Was it left there for
later? If so, how was it used later? Maybe this ties into the concept
of last orders for a given scale.

2. Should I even chase entries below the neckline? If so what should I
be looking for? Is it just down to MM or are there clues in price that I
 should be following?

 orders, order flow and transactions

1. Some concepts that seem to be at the core of Sali's trading. Interesting, need more study.

Scale

1. Heh, what else can I say. It's hard, need deliberate practice.

And the theory. Its been said many times that price simply goes from FL
 to FL. Engulfs of these FLs (whatever these engulf signals are)
indicate the ITs are ready to move price to the next level. Footprints
are left behind in the form of mpl/qm/ls levels of remaining orders and
ultimately, where price will turn. Reversal signals and tricks will be
played as we approach these orders. The more orders they have to fill,
the more tricks will have to be played. And we tie these signals
through scale to get the complete picture. That seems to be pretty much
 it, no? But the trick is to accurately identify these signals,
especially in real time. And that's where I think I need to go back and
 fully understand FLs, how they're engulfed, the footprints left behind,
 and targets, as they seem to be the fundamental framework for what we
do.

Wow that was a lot more questions than i thought I had. Probably left a
 few out too. I feel like before I've been frustrating with not trading
 because that's where 'true' learning happens. But now I feel like true
 learning happens when you have full grasp of the concepts, and using
the market to test out your theories. You, Sali and many others before
us has showed us you can read the market to the pip, so that is now my
goal, and the material is all here. Whether i reach it or not, I will
become better through it's journey. As always, thanks for everything
you've provided us IF! Now time to get

the origin, QM, or MPL level and boom! I will post some charts of trades
 in the following weeks. Here's hoping that the mind doesnt throw more
obstacles in the way.

my main points, it can be subjective! If you don't mark a line and
price bounces from it's kink, oh well plenty of opportunities. If you
do highlight a line where price doesn't bounce, then you have approach
(and validation) to confirm the trade. Just learn from it and refine
the process through your experience. Just like any other concept here
on RTM.

But for the sake of debate, lets talk about that line. You're right

reason that's important, especially on a monthly, is because that
would've been a line on the quarterly chart! For me i don't mind tight
line clusters like that, it just tells me that general area is
important.
